A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete 38-page contents, including equations, figures, tables, Appendices A–H, and checklists, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GPT-2/SST-2 and CIFAR-10 experiments, privacy-bound comparisons, Census-risk analyses, and simulations of private query answering in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental, simulation, and data-analysis results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The unified f-DP risk analysis and attack-aware noise-calibration procedures remain unchanged. Appendix D revises mathematical statements without reporting a changed computational procedure or model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian/Laplace scenarios, SST-2 sentiment classification, CIFAR-10 image classification, Census releases, binary inference setting, and private query-answering simulation.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Cohen and Nissim's PSO bounds, Balle et al.'s reconstruction bounds, Guo et al.'s analytical and Monte Carlo Fano bounds, and the standard smartnoise composition comparison.

E3.justification: The reported splits, noise settings, adjacency relations, risk metrics, model configurations, and training budgets are unchanged. Appendix G retains identical experimental parameter tables.

E4.justification: The Bernoulli-prior comparison, alternative-baseline analyses, query-answering case study, and supplementary PSO comparisons are retained. The revised Appendix D theorem does not introduce a new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains 10,000 Monte Carlo samples, ten repetitions, and the statement that its error bars are not visible. No uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: The plotted results and reported findings are unchanged, including the SST-2 accuracy comparison of 52% versus 70%, CIFAR-10 comparison of 65% versus 68%, and query-answering comparison of 5 versus 15 queries. Relocated appendix figures retain their results.

T1.justification: Appendix D substantively revises two specialized results. Proposition D.1 replaces R_f(π) ≤ π+(1−π)δ(logit(π)) with R_f(π) ≥ (1−π)[1−δ(logit(π))]. Theorem D.1 replaces arbitrary bounded q with explicitly complementary binary scores and rewrites its proof, including changing the final inequality to equality. The main unified bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified and tunable privacy-risk bounds, tighter estimates than prior approaches, utility benefits from noise calibration, and generalization/memorization consequences.

C2.justification: Appendix D now explicitly presents its specialized result as a binary SAI/SMIA success bound and explains the complementary-score requirement, narrowing its stated applicability. The main tightness discussion and limitations concerning privacy units and baseline gaming remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same hyperparameters, hardware and runtime information, software list, riskcal code-release link, and supplementary-code disclosure. No additional implementation or access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Adding 'Based on' to Proposition D.1's existing Sason and Verdú attribution and clarifying the TPDP workshop description are limited wording refinements.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and terminology edits, standardizes appendix references, clarifies threat-model exposition, and adds Swiss National Science Foundation acknowledgments. The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's annotations, legend, and sizing are adjusted. Appendix reflow relocates Figure 5, Figure 7, and Table 1, while preserving their content and structure. Equation spacing and presentation also change.

improvement.justification: v3 improves Appendix D by removing Theorem D.1's unjustified arbitrary-function generality and providing a Bayes-error lower bound in Proposition D.1. These are useful localized repairs. However, the revised proof newly asserts a final equality without establishing an optimizing attack score, so proof correctness is not fully resolved. The main framework and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
